findings.title: audit-changes.toml's anchor flags contradict the D18 they cite
locations: catalog/lanes/audit-changes.toml:3 — "diffstat arrive in args. † anchors are constants (D18)."
catalog/lanes/audit-changes.toml:22,38,44,78 — anchor = true on under-rejection, behaviour-change, over-rejection, contract-drift

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:923-925 (D18) — "engine lanes carry it in the catalogue as a constant (the `executing` audit lane, the two free hunt lanes, the dismissal auditor and the severity re-check are `anchor = true` there)"
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2086-2088 — restates the identical list a second time
docs/design-record/survey-bughunt-auditchanges.md:233 — "IT five (executing, under-rejection, behaviour-change, over-rejection, contract-drift)" — the set actually shipped
findings.description: The catalogue file's own comment says its `anchor` column instantiates D18. But D18, stated twice in ARCHITECTURE.md in near-identical wording, names only the `executing` lane as an anchor among the audit-changes lanes (plus the two free hunt lanes, the dismissal auditor and the severity re-check — none of which are audit-changes rows). The shipped file actually marks FIVE audit-changes lanes anchor=true: executing, under-rejection, behaviour-change, over-rejection and contract-drift. The design-record survey shows this five-lane set was the deliberate IT-derived choice (over PF's rival five, which swapped `invariants` for `over-rejection`), so the catalogue itself looks like the intended, adopted state — it is ARCHITECTURE.md's D18 paragraph that under-lists what it claims to define exhaustively. Either way, one of the two texts a reader is told to treat as authoritative is currently wrong about the other, and the catalogue's own citation of D18 is the false claim as written.
findings.resolution_hint: Expand D18's parenthetical (both occurrences, ARCHITECTURE.md:923-925 and :2086-2088) to name all five audit-changes anchors (executing, under-rejection, behaviour-change, over-rejection, contract-drift), or drop the `(D18)` citation from catalog/lanes/audit-changes.toml:3 if the anchor set is no longer meant to be read off that paragraph.

findings.title: doc-policy and naming-policy carry a `source` grant their persona text never invokes
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/panel.js:86 — the `source` grant's payoff: "ALSO the AUTHORED SOURCE (read it with Read/Grep; quote findings at file:line)"
catalog/hats/invariants-and-decisions.toml:111 — the sibling rulebook hat that DOES use its `source` grant: "check the invariants and decision log against the code and docs BOTH WAYS"
catalog/hats/latex-typesetter.toml:120 — another `source`-needing hat that explicitly instructs "quote each finding at its SOURCE file:line"
findings.description: Of the three catalogue "rulebook hats" (naming-policy, doc-policy, invariants-and-decisions — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:417, design-record/05-fix-rulings.md:9), all three carry `needs = ["rulebook", "source"]`, and every other hat that carries a `source` grant (fossil-and-drift, latex-typesetter) explicitly tells the hat to open src/ext and quote file:line. invariants-and-decisions does too ("against the code"). doc-policy and naming-policy do not: their checklists (docstring section order/shape; public-name meaning and uniqueness) are entirely answerable from the rendered manuscript their `full` substrate already grants, and their own output instructions ask only for a quoted rule/name, never a file:line. The `source` grant on these two looks copied uniformly across the three rulebook hats rather than set per hat's actual need.
findings.resolution_hint: Either add a sentence to doc-policy's and naming-policy's persona text that uses the source grant (e.g. verifying a docstring's displayed section order against the raw `"""..."""` source rather than the rendered page), or drop `"source"` from their `needs` lists if the rendered manuscript alone suffices.
